entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Dou Xian (died 92 CE) was a pivotal military figure and powerful consort kin of the Eastern Han dynasty, whose decisive campaigns fundamentally reshaped the geopolitical landscape of East Asia by eliminating the long-standing threat posed by the Northern Xiongnu confederation. As the brother of Empress Dou, his extraordinary influence allowed him to orchestrate grand expeditions that stretched from the Han frontier into the heart of the Gobi Desert and beyond the Altai Mountains, marking a critical turning point in the protracted Han-Xiongnu Wars that had defined Chinese foreign policy for over two centuries.

Dou Xian's most celebrated achievements occurred between 89 and 91 CE. In 89 CE, leading a massive Han army of 50,000 cavalry, he launched a devastating offensive from Jilu against the Northern Xiongnu, routing their forces at the Battle of Ikh Bayan (near present-day Zagaan Nuur, Mongolia) and pursuing them deep into the Gobi Desert. This victory compelled the Northern Chanyu (leader) to flee westward and effectively shattered the Xiongnu's organized resistance, resulting in over 13,000 enemy casualties and the submission of over 81 tribes. Two years later, in 91 CE, Dou Xian dispatched a final expedition that chased the remaining Northern Xiongnu elements further west across the Altai Mountains, forcing their Chanyu to migrate into Central Asia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dou Xian's military campaigns fundamentally altered the power balance in East Asia by eliminating the Northern Xiongnu, a dominant nomadic power for centuries, and securing Han control over crucial Central Asian trade routes. This action enabled a subsequent century of relative peace on the northern frontier and expanded Han influence deep into the Western Regions.
